title: SLO Governance Playbook for Cross-Functional Flywheel
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook that frames SLO governance as an operational "flywheel"—a repeating set of practices that improves service reliability through continuous partnership between product, platform, SRE, and CS. The goal: make SLO decisions fast, observable, reversible, and low-friction for feature teams while preserving system-wide safety nets.

Status & audience:
- Draft (working notes + tentative timeline).
- Primary readers: SRE leads, product managers for feature teams, platform engineers, reliability liaisons.
- Secondary: Solutions Eng, Customer Success for escalations.

High-level flywheel stages (4-step):
1) Discover & Instrument: define user-facing signal, measurement method, and owners.
2) Agree & Commit: negotiate SLO thresholds, error budgets, and escalation contracts.
3) Operate & Observe: enforce rollouts, monitor spend of error budget, run automation.
4) Learn & Iterate: postmortems, calibration, and push back into instrumentation.

Principles (short):
- Minimize decision latency: spec + SLO review should fit a single 2-week sprint when low-risk.
- Prefer observable, deterministic signals over heuristics.
- Keep rollback paths simple and automated.
- Error budget policies must be predictable and fair across teams.
- Reuse runbook components and measurement pipelines where possible.

Minimum artifacts for an SLO onramp:
- Owner: service/product/infra owner (name + rotation contact).
- Customer impact statement: 1–2 sentence description of what users notice when this fails.
- Primary signal: metric name, tags, aggregation window, sampling rate (e.g., api.v1.generate.success_rate, 5m window).
- Measurement doc: metric query, dashboard id, alert definitions (thresholds & windows).
- SLO target and time-window (e.g., 99.5% over 30d).
- Error budget policy: automatic throttles, rate-limited feature flags, canary gating rules.
- Rollback policy and runbook link (existing template).

Roles & responsibilities (RACI-ish):
- Feature Team (R): propose SLO, provide customer impact context, instrument code.
- SRE (A): validate measurement, approve SLI, define alert to SLO mapping, own runbook templates.
- Platform (C): ensure platform-level metrics (GPU/memory/queues) are available, support autoscaling hooks.
- Product/PM (C): sign-off threshold that aligns to business risk.
- Reliability Liaison (I): weekly status updates, coordinates cross-team mitigation.
- Exec Sponsor (I): for escalations beyond error budget throttles.

Cadence & meetings:
- Weekly SLO triage (30m): review services with >5% error budget burn this week. Attendees: SRE leads, reliability liaisons, rotating feature team rep.
- Monthly SLO calibration (60m): review slow-moving SLOs, adjustments, and strategic tradeoffs. Attendees include product leadership.
- Pre-release SLO checkpoint (ad-hoc 15–30m): before canary to prod for features that could materially affect SLOs.

Implementation checklist (first 90 days for an individual service):
Week 0–2:
- Draft customer impact statement and proposed SLI.
- Add metric to observability backend; create dashboard stub.
- Create a PR: measurement docs + queries (link PR in linked_artifacts).
Week 3–4:
- SRE reviews measurement accuracy and confirms cardinality/perf impact.
- Agree SLO target; draft error budget policy.
Week 5–8:
- Wire up automation: error budget burn alerts -> Slack + PagerDuty if >X%/24h.
- Configure automated canary rollback gates / feature-flag throttle.
Week 9–12:
- Run a simulated burn tabletop (10–15m script) with SRE and FE.
- Postmortem template: run after any error budget exhaustion incident.

Operational patterns and examples:
- Canary gating: if canary cohort sees >2% relative drop in success_rate (5m window), auto-rollback. Config lives in platform/ff-service: canary-gates.yaml.
- Progressive throttling: when error budget burn exceeds 20% in 24h, apply 10% traffic shed to non-critical endpoints (configurable route lists).
- Fallback models: route to smaller-quantized model if latency SLO is violated and return correctness within tolerance. (Tie to model catalog)
content_continued:
Monitoring & alerts (practical):
- Alert tiers: informational (burn <10%), operational (10–30%), incident (>=30% or >50% in any 24h).
- Alert sinks: Slack channel #slo-{service}, PagerDuty rotation, and SLO-triage board (JIRA filter).
- Dashboard essentials: SLI time series, error budget remaining (visualized as %), top contributing endpoints/error types, latency P95/P99.

Runbooks & automation snippets (notes-to-self):
- Template runbook sections: Overview, Symptoms, Quick mitigation steps (toggle FF, rollback), Deeper diagnostics (logs & traces), Postmortem checklist.
- Auto-mitigation playbook (sketch): 1) notify product + SRE; 2) if burnout persists 15m -> execute traffic shed; 3) disable feature flag; 4) escalate to exec if customer SLA impacted.

Cross-team dependencies & risk map:
- Observability infra (high): metric cardinality and ingestion quotas can block accurate SLI measurement. Mitigation: platform commits dedicated ingestion budget for onboarding services.
- Model serving runtime (medium): model fallbacks require compatibility testing. Mitigation: model compatibility matrix + preflight tests in CI.
- Billing/quotas (low-medium): throttling can interact with rate limits billed to customers—coordinate with finance for high-impact customers.

Measurement quality guidance (to avoid bad SLOs):
- Avoid noisy signals (use 5m or 1m smoothing based on traffic).
- Choose signals tied to user-experienced errors (e.g., reply==empty, status!=200).
- Limit high-cardinality tags in SLI queries or pre-aggregate with service-side counters.

Decision heuristics (how we change SLOs):
- If daily recurring infra incidents cause >15% monthly error budget usage for 3 months, recommend raising platform investment before lowering SLO.
- SLO relaxations require product + SRE sign-off and a 30-day observational window post-change.
- SLO tightenings need incremental canary + 60-day monitoring with rollback gating.

Playbook metrics to track success of the governance flywheel:
- Time from SLO proposal -> approved (target: <2 sprints).
- % of services with automated mitigation (target: 70% within 6 months).
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for SLO breaches.
- Frequency of false-positive SLO alerts.

Open questions / TODOs (backlog):
- [ ] Finalize standard error budget policy YAML schema and store in repo platform/slo-policies/. (owner: Morgan)
- [ ] Decide default SLO targets per class (critical/important/low) — propose by product taxonomy (owner: Product)
- [ ] Add a low-friction SLO onboarding form (internal web form) that auto-opens a JIRA ticket. (owner: DevEx)
- [ ] Evaluate cost of increased metric retention for SLI accuracy. (owner: Observability)
- [ ] Draft exec escalation template for customer-impacting SLO burns >72h. (owner: Rina)

Notes & recent meeting snippets (informal):
- 2026-02-10 SLO triage: discussed API v2 intermittent 5xx pattern; agreed short-term mitigation to shard requests + patch. Action: Samir to add traffic-shift playbook.
- 2026-02-15 Calibration: product asked for 99.9 for onboarding API; SRE recommended 99.5 with plan to instrument deeper traces first. Product to pilot 99.9 in a bounded canary.

Appendix — Useful links (placeholders):
- SLO templates: confluence.company.com/display/RELIABILITY/SLO+Templates
- Runbook template PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/4182
- JIRA SLO triage board: https://jira.company/browse/SRE-BOARD

Bottom line / thesis (1 sentence):
Treat SLO governance as an iterating flywheel: reduce friction for teams to create and operate SLOs while building platform-level guardrails that stop single services from causing systemic risk.
